 JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 25,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6453/2018 That on 14.04.2018 at about 8.45 a.m, when the Petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on TVS Moped bearing Reg.No.KA41S3004 and they reached near Telecom Layout, Railway gate, Telecom layout road, Bengaluru, at that time, one Maruthi Ritz Car bearing Reg.No.KA01AF8918 driven by its driver came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to which the Petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Baptist hospital, Hebbal and after first aid treatment, he was shifted to NIMHANS and Bowring hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient. Thereafter, he was shifted to Prolife Hospital for further treatment.
He spent more than Rs.5,00,000/ towards medicines and Rs.1,50,000/ towards incidental charges.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a Painter and was earning SCCH 15 4 MVC No.6453/2018 750/ per day.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Maruthi Ritz Car bearing Reg.No.KA01AF 8918 by its driver.

The Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and therefore both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.2 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.1 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1 in its Objection statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.6453/2018 expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

If so, what amount & from whom ?

16. P.W.1 is subjected for crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1.
In the cross examination nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has examined Senior Manager by name Suresh as RW.1 and he got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4 i.e., Notarized SCCH 15 11 MVC No.6453/2018 copy of Policy,
Charge sheet, Copy of Notice and Returned RPAD cover with Notice.

Though the Respondent No.1 contended that there is a Contributory Negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle wherein the Petitioner was travelled, the Spot Sketch shows the rider of the motorcycle has already reached near center median.

Further, the IMV report i.e., Ex.P5 shows the front Bumper (right) bonnet damage found on the offending vehicle and the Rear registration number board right rear indicator damages found on the motorcycle of the Petitioner, which clearly indicates that the rider of the motorcycle already crossed the road and then the offending car dashed to the rear portion of the motorcycle.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Maruthi Ritz Car bearing Reg.No.KA01AF8918 by its driver and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
SCCH 15 12 MVC No.6453/2018 17. Issue No.2: As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
21.
The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P6 issued by the Medical Officer of the Prolife Multi Speciality hospital, Bengaluru, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P8 - Discharge summary shows the Petitioner was diagnosed for Poly Trauma with Pelvic fracture, AKI stage III Sec to ATN requiring HD (Recovered) and B/L ectopic kidney.

22. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding SCCH 15 14 MVC No.6453/2018 compensation of 75,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
23.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
24.

The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at Prolife hospital,
Bengaluru.
Upon going through Ex.P.8  Discharge summary of Prolife hospital shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 19.04.2018 to 23.05.2018.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 35 days.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as four months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 50,000/ under this head (@ 12,500/ per month ).
IV.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
26.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 12,000/ (@ 100/ per day) towards attendants charges, 12,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 12,000/ towards conveyance would be just SCCH 15 16 MVC No.6453/2018 and reasonable.

In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 36,000/
under this head.

sentences.text: COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
27. The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent more than Rs.6,50,000/ towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills and hospital bills marked at Ex.P11 amounting to Rs.6,89,558/.
I have gone through the same and the same is acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.6,89,600/.

Hence,
I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,89,600/ under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

28. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6453/2018 disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

29. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him.
Further, he assessed the whole body disability of the Petitioner at 16%.
PW.2 got marked Clinical note and Xray at Ex.P14 and 15.
In the crossexamination, PW.2 admitted that he has not treated the Petitioner and he has not seen the old medical records of the Petitioner.
He further admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner was united.

He further admitted that the disability sustained by the Petitioner can be cured in the further treatment and there might be chance of changes in the assessment of disability after getting physiotherapy treatment.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6453/2018 the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
30. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of 12,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,80,000/ ( 12,500/ x 12 =
1,50,000/, 1,92,000/x 15 x 8/100 = 1,80,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,80,000/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
31.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering 75,000/ SCCH 15 19 MVC No.6453/2018 2. Loss of amenities  50,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid up  50,000/ period 4.

Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  36,000/ and conveyance Shivachand vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co., Ltd on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51646100/
7 5.

Medical expenses 6,89,600/
6. Loss of Future Income 1,80,000/ Total Rs.10,80,600/
32.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.10,80,600/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

32. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Maruthi Ritz Car bearing Reg.No.KA01AF8918.

The Respondent No.1 taken contention that the driver of the offending vehicle did not hold DL at the time of accident and also it contended that the Respondent No.2 being the owner of SCCH 15 20 MVC No.6453/2018 the offending vehicle knowingly entrusted his vehicle to the driver, who did not hold effective driving license at the time of alleged accident.

In order to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions, it examined its Senior Manager by name Suresh as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4 i.e., Copy of Policy, Charge sheet, Notice issued to the owner of the offending vehicle and the Returned RPAD.
Ex.R3 shows that Notice was issued to the owner of the vehicle i.e., Respondent No.2 asking all particulars of the vehicle and also DL particulars of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Ex.R4 is the Returned RPAD which returned with shara as "left the address, hence returned".
Hence, it shows that the Respondent No.1 Insurance Company has made an attempt to get the details of the DL particulars of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 has relied on Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA SCCH 15 21 MVC No.6453/2018 No.3297/2019 dated 13.04.2023, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to observed as under:
"Not possessing driving license is a valid ground for the Insurance Company to succeed and in the instant case, the rider was not possessing valid and effective driving license.

The owner who consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving license, cannot take the benefit of his own wrong, and the insurance company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of MV Act."

33. Further it has observed that "The Respondent No.1 / insured did not choose to contest the matter and it is evident from the records, especially the reply given by Respondent No.1 / owner, the rider was not possessing valid and effective driving license."

Hence, it pleased to held that the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is a clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on Respondent No.1 / owner himself.
At this juncture, I would like to rely on the decision of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.4716/2011(MV) SCCH 15 22 MVC No.6453/2018

in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd.,
Vs. Smt. Umamaheshwari @ Umadevi and others and MFA No.6154/2019 (MVD) in between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.,

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to discussed regarding liability, when the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the driving license and it has pleased to observed in Shivachand vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co., Ltd on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51646100/
8 the said Judgment that the Respondent No.2  the owner of the vehicle neither contested the petition by filing Written Statement nor adduced any evidence claiming that he did not consciously permit the rider of the vehicle to ride the vehicle.

entities.text: Shivachand vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co., Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, it pleased to observed that "The rider of the vehicle without driving license was not impeached by him.

Hence, the Tribunal was justified in holding that the Respondent No.2 permitted operating of the vehicle by an unauthorized person and the said act of Respondent No.2 amounts to fundamental breach of policy SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6453/2018 condition within the meaning of Sec.149(2)(a)(ii) of the MV Act.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in exonerating the insurer on the ground that there is fundamental breach of policy condition."

34. In the instant case, the Chargesheet Ex.P7 and Ex.R2 clearly shows that the driver of the offending vehicle was Chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.

Further, the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., Respondent No.2 was Chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sec.5(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act for knowingly entrusted the offending vehicle to the driver, who did not possess the driving license.

Moreover, he did not appear before the Court and he was placed exparte.
35.

Hence, in this case also the Respondent No.2 did not contest the matter and the Respondent No.2 being the owner knowingly entrusted the offending vehicle to the Petitioner who did not possessing the DL.
Hence, there is a clear breach of policy condition.
Therefore, the insurer is not liable to pay SCCH 15 24 MVC No.6453/2018 compensation to the Petitioner.

On the other hand,
the Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
36. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.10,80,600/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay  the compensation amount to the  Petitioner.
